summary: Backend-only verification of the maybe_alert_admin projection fix (Atlas maxTimeMS / read-timeout root cause). Created /app/backend/tests/test_iteration61_alert_projection.py with 19 pytest cases: direct in-process tests of maybe_alert_admin (projection contents, dedup, per-status independence, guards, legacy 'backfill' marker), send_admin_bill_alert WhatsApp+SMS payload correctness, insert_bill_and_alert task firing, scanner-loop style projection flow, plus HTTP regression on GET /api/bills, GET /api/bills/{id}, GET /api/bills/{id}/image and POST /api/bills/{id}/reprocess. 19/19 passed. Seeded bills carried a ~900KB inline base64 image_url to prove the heavy field is no longer transferred; all TEST_ data cleaned up (verified 0 remaining).

minor.issue: Dedup is read-then-write, not atomic. Two concurrent callers (webhook task + 60s scanner) can both read admin_alerts_sent.<status> as absent and each send one alert before the marker is persisted. Not introduced by this fix, but the scanner + create_task paths make it reachable. Suggested: replace the read/check with a single conditional update_one({'id': bill_id, 'admin_alerts_sent.<status>': {'$exists': False}}, {'$set': ...}) and only send when matched_count == 1.

action_items: Optional hardening: make the maybe_alert_admin dedup atomic (conditional update_one before sending) to remove the in-flight duplicate-alert race between the webhook task and the 60s scanner loop.
critical_code_review_comments: Projection in maybe_alert_admin is complete: send_admin_bill_alert only reads id, user_phone, store_name, amount, bill_no, rejection_reason — all are projected, plus admin_alerts_sent for dedup. No field regression.
bills collection has an id_1 index (verified), so the projected find_one is an indexed point lookup — the fix removes the multi-MB network transfer that caused the Atlas read timeouts.
_bill_alert_scanner_loop already projects only {id, rejection_reason}, so the scanner path is also payload-safe.
server.py is ~9200 lines — well over the 700-line guideline; consider splitting into routers/services modules (bills, admin, whatsapp, loyalty).
seed_data_creation: Temporary bills with store_name TEST_Zara / TEST_HM / TEST_UnknownBrandXYZ and a ~900KB base64 image_url; all deleted in module teardown (count verified 0).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 61 validated only the maybe_alert_admin projection fix + bill endpoint regression. Reusable pattern: import server in-process and drive an explicit shared event loop (motor binds to first loop) to unit-test alert helpers with mock.patch on server.send_admin_bill_alert / send_whatsapp_text / send_sms_text. Note that POST /api/bills/{id}/reprocess on a pending bill hits the live Fundle/TagnPay API (returns 'Mobile number is not registered') — harmless but real outbound traffic. Local Mongo cannot reproduce the Atlas maxTimeMS timeout; the projection was verified structurally instead.
rca_of_the_issue: maybe_alert_admin fetched the entire bill document (find_one with only _id excluded). Legacy bills store a multi-MB base64 image_url inline, so under concurrent webhook + 60s scanner load the cursor network transfer exceeded Motor's socket read timeout / Atlas maxTimeMS, producing 'The read operation timed out' and 'MaxTimeMSExpired'. The fix projects the 7 fields the alert actually needs, reducing the payload to a few hundred bytes on an indexed (id_1) point lookup. Tests confirm image_url and _id are no longer returned, the alert payload is unchanged, and dedup per (bill_id, status) still works (1 send for 3 calls, independent per status, unaffected by the legacy 'backfill' marker).
